Run a FLOP validator or GPU miner

Start with the role you want to operate. These instructions describe the repository's current development workflows, reviewed on 2026-09-29. They do not announce a public network launch or certify a currently running network. The validator rehearsal and the GPU miner deployment require their own matching network configuration; do not combine presets from separate networks.

RoleWhat you runStart hereEvidence of success
ValidatorCPU node for BABE authoring and AlephBFT finality, plus its configured DA service; no GPU/TEE requiredValidator setupActive session/BABE/Aleph keys and advancing finality
GPU minerGPU inference backend plus a distinct miner worker/account, on one or more owned or rented GPU hosts; SOFT development pathMiner setupReal inference, finalized registration, accepted calibration, then accepted work, first host before the next

Owning or renting GPUs and mining are one role. Renting out GPU capacity alone does not make anyone a FLOP miner: whoever operates the measured inference stack owns its account, funds the required deposits and completes registration and calibration. GPU owners new to crypto can start with Put your GPU to work on FLOP. Likewise, a healthy validator container is not evidence that the chain admitted its account.

Inputs you need before starting

Obtain a network-specific operator release from the network administrator. Keep the following values together so a setup cannot silently mix incompatible versions:

  • Network identity: network name, expected genesis hash, chain spec or supported preset, bootstrap peer multiaddrs and accessible RPC. Check the actual genesis hash before signing.
  • Software: source revision, immutable node/worker/backend image digests, supported host architecture, release checksums and upgrade compatibility information.
  • Access: how the host reaches the RPC, chain proxy, DA and any approved private network; which services require credentials and who issues them. Never paste secrets into chat.
  • Admission: operator public account, current stake requirement, fee funding and any administrator-only funding/promotion or calibration issuer step. Keys stay with their owner.
  • Miner model: onboarded modelpack hash, exact checkpoint revision, decode policy, storage requirements and independent calibration-job service.

The guides provide commands, configuration fields and acceptance criteria. Some supporting artifacts and addresses are still private or not released. An empty input is a blocked step, not permission to invent a hostname, image, chain identifier or model hash.

Private URL placeholders

Any hostname ending in .invalid, or value labelled REPLACE_WITH_…, is a placeholder. It will not connect to FLOP. Replace it only with the administrator's verified value. A placeholder table is a handoff contract, not an announcement that the service exists.

InputExample placeholderWhat the administrator supplies
Release bundlehttps://releases.flop.invalid/operator/Versioned artifacts, checksums and supported network
Chain RPCwss://rpc.flop.invalidReachable endpoint, access method and expected genesis hash
Bootstrap peer/dns4/boot.flop.invalid/tcp/30333/p2p/REPLACE_WITH_PEER_IDReachable P2P multiaddr and peer identity
Image registryregistry.flop.invalid/flop/node@sha256:REPLACE_WITH_DIGESTPull access and immutable digest
Operator supporthttps://operators.flop.invalid/supportSupport portal. None is published. Devnet validators still pass administrator review (Run a validator); request what only an operator grants with an access request.

Loopback addresses in the guides are actual local service bindings, not public service URLs. Never expose unsafe node RPC, session tokens or a raw inference backend to the Internet merely to make a health check pass.

Let an agent handle the setup

FLOP publishes two reviewed Agent Skills, setup-validator and setup-miner. Install one with the command on the operator reference page, which also shows each file's SHA-256; Run a FLOP miner has the miner command and prompt. The source release carries the same files under .agents/skills/. Then ask a compatible coding agent:

> Use setup-validator to set up my FLOP validator on the supplied host. Use the supplied > release and network configuration, gather missing non-secret inputs together, preserve > existing data, complete the authorized setup, and report admission and finality evidence.

Or:

> Use setup-miner to set up my GPU host as a FLOP SOFT miner. Use the supplied model and network > release, gather missing non-secret inputs together, keep secrets on the host, and report > inference, registration, calibration and accepted-work evidence separately.

Include the host, network, desired role, release location and authorized spending/signing scope. Install or provide the skill file if the agent cannot discover it; a skill name alone does not download instructions. Do not give an agent your wallet seed in a conversation. Existing operator authorization covers routine setup; a new paid rental, account funding or administrator signature needs the corresponding owner's authority.

“One go” means one coordinated setup workflow. Chain session transitions, calibration windows, missing artifacts and external admission can prevent immediate completion. The agent must return the exact remaining gate instead of claiming that the host is earning.

Readiness and maintenance

Validator administrator actions use the applicant's public address for funding, promotion, refresh and verification; only the applicant's local join needs its seed. Follow Run a FLOP validator to keep applicant and administrator credentials on their respective hosts.

Keep a receipt with the release/image digests, network/genesis, public account, configuration locations, running service versions, finalized transaction references and role-specific checks. Redact private endpoints when sharing it. Back up local configuration and keystores securely; never run two validators with the same session keys. For miners, preserve model/cache and required evidence data and recheck gateway/session identity after a restart.

Upgrade one host first using a supported pinned release, then repeat the same checks before expanding the rollout. Container uptime alone cannot establish protocol readiness. Follow the role guide's shutdown and recovery steps; deleting a volume is not routine repair.

Known blockers and follow-up work

These issues track release gaps that an operator cannot repair by changing URLs:

  • Public operator release bundle (#2003): source/image/model/network packaging and a clean-host acceptance drill.
  • Miner hot-key delegation (#913) and session-key persistence (#1977): avoid treating a funded account on a rented host as an isolated disposable worker key.
  • SOFT model onboarding (#2004): the CLI offers flop model onboard --soft without a TEE claim, but a new model still needs its modelpack root, decode policy, and live backend capture validated. A real local/devnet registration and discovery proof remains to close the issue. Follow Run a FLOP miner for the command and the validated devnet model.
  • SOFT settlement/disputes (#650): the current development workflow is not a complete production earning guarantee. HARD is also not currently deployable from this repository.

The issue numbers refer to FLOP's private repository, so they are not links. The requirements and limitations needed to follow these guides are stated here and in each role guide.
